suggestions.assertion: Reusa tokens --bus-* existentes em vez de introduzir hex novos pros papéis (fundo/borda/texto/sombra) que já têm token
suggestions.reason: This assertion is somewhat under-specified in a way that made grading require external verification rather than transcript/output-only checking: it says 'papéis que já têm token', but strictly by --bus-* custom-property tokens alone, neither '#3557C4' (metro blue) nor accent-text white has a --bus-* CSS variable — they only have pre-existing hardcoded literals elsewhere in globals.css. A model could satisfy the letter of the assertion (introduce zero new --bus-* near-duplicates) while still not noticing the file already has raw hex baked into several classes, so a stricter/cleaner version of this assertion might explicitly also check 'or reuses an existing literal/class already used for the same semantic role in this file' to reward this kind of consistency-driven reuse rather than just token-lookup reuse.

No assertion checks the empty/loading-state redesign (skeleton cards replacing the spinner) even though this is one of the more Uber-like, substantively 'premium polish' changes in the diff (SUMMARY.md items 7-8). It would be worth an assertion verifying the loading state was upgraded beyond a bare spinner, since this is a meaningful, easily-graded outcome that speaks directly to the 'nível do Uber' framing of the prompt and is currently unchecked.

No assertion checks for accessibility/contrast regressions or reduced-motion handling (e.g. prefers-reduced-motion) despite adding six new keyframe-driven animations (slideUp entrance, favPop, livePulse, skeletonShimmer, plus hover/active transforms) — a genuinely Uber-level polish pass would typically respect prefers-reduced-motion, and this run does not (no such media query appears in the CSS diff). This is an outcome I observed that no assertion currently catches, worth considering for a future iteration of this eval.

eval_feedback.overall: All 5 assertions pass with solid, non-coincidental evidence in changes.diff and SUMMARY.md — this baseline (no-skill) run happened to already follow the design system's token conventions closely, correctly reused existing keyframes/tokens, used a custom (non-linear) cubic-bezier for the signature entrance animation, and produced a real, substantial code diff. The two new hex literals introduced ('#3557C4', '#FFFFFF') were checked individually against the actual globals.css palette and both turned out to be exact reuses of pre-existing values/patterns already present in the codebase for the same semantic roles, not new near-duplicate inventions — so the passes reflect genuine care, not luck. That said, this is a notably strong result for a 'without_skill' baseline; if this pattern holds across other iteration-1 tasks it may indicate these particular assertions are not very discriminating between skill and no-skill runs on this prompt, since a reasonably careful general-purpose agent already tends to grep the existing design tokens before adding new colors on a task this explicitly about 'reusing an existing app's card' rather than building from scratch.
